## Item 12 — Opt-in off-app delivery for the recurring due-date reminder ([Item 1](#item-1--recurring-due-date-reminder-notification-un-deferred-from-deferredmd-item-40) / [ADR-0052](../adr/0052-recurring-due-date-reminder-foreground.md))

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `f26a951`** 2026-07-28 (Opus/xhigh — Alvin's explicit override of the booked Sonnet/medium) — built, `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` (1226) green, on-device verified 11/11 with **one real bug found and fixed** (see Build outcome). Grilled + design-locked 2026-07-28 ([ADR-0056](../adr/0056-off-app-recurring-reminder-periodic-sweep.md)). **Booked as: Sonnet, medium effort** — the grill collapsed this the same way Items 1 and 9 collapsed: the Opus-shaped questions (does this reverse ADR-0012? does it need alarm infrastructure?) are answered and cost nothing structural. What's left is one pure function, a second registration of an existing worker, four teardown call sites, and a banner. **Medium rather than low only because of the lifecycle points** — the sign-out cancel is the kind of thing that passes every test and silently leaks a forever-schedule. *That prediction landed almost exactly: the bug found on-device was a lifecycle call site that passed every test and silently failed to re-arm.* **No schema/Room/Supabase change.**
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-27):** while confirming the recurring reminder only fires on app-open/sync (by design, ADR-0052), Alvin asked for an **opt-in** option so it can also fire without opening the app — with the **current foreground/sync-triggered behavior staying the default**.
- **Why now:** ADR-0052's own Consequences section anticipated this exact ask: *"If tester feedback shows off-app reach is genuinely missed, a real alarm can be added later as its own grilled item, born aware of the force-stop-ROM caveat above."*

### Grill outcome (2026-07-28) — full design resolved, [ADR-0056](../adr/0056-off-app-recurring-reminder-periodic-sweep.md)

**Three codebase findings reframed the item before any decision was made:**

1. **ADR-0052's central objection was overstated.** It argued off-app scheduling "cuts against ADR-0012's foreground-only posture" — but [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-interactive-in-process-background-workmanager.md)'s own decision text assigns WorkManager *"the deferrable/reliable paths: retry-with-backoff…, the network-reconnect trigger, and **any periodic sweep**."* A `PeriodicWorkRequest` is therefore explicitly **within** ADR-0012, not against it; what ADR-0012 forbids is routing *interactive* work through WorkManager, and what v1.6.6 Item 36 declined was periodic background **sync** (a product call), not periodic work as a mechanism. ADR-0052 evaluated `AlarmManager` and rejected it correctly — it never evaluated a periodic worker at all. ADR-0052 is amended with this correction.
2. **The reminder check needs zero network.** [ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/domain/usecase/ObservePendingConfirmationsUseCase.kt#L44) derives pending occurrences purely from local Room (rules × categories × materialized ids). Off-app delivery needs no sync, no `CONNECTED` constraint, works in airplane mode.
3. **The notification workers are *cold-launch* triggered, not app-open triggered.** All three (`BudgetAlertWorker`, `RecurringReminderWorker`, `PartnerDebtNotificationWorker`) are enqueued only from `MainActivity`'s `LaunchedEffect(current.userId)` — once per process launch — and the tail of a completed `SyncWorker` (itself enqueued at login and by the widget ⟳). The `onStart` observer syncs in-process but enqueues no workers. Reopening from recents without the process dying re-checks nothing.

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Mechanism** | **`PeriodicWorkRequest` targeting the existing `RecurringReminderWorker`** — no `AlarmManager`, no `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`, no new manifest permission, no new worker class. ADR-0052's `AlarmManager` rejection **stands, reaffirmed on stronger grounds**: inexact alarms lose their schedule on reboot (needs a boot receiver + reschedule-on-every-rule-change); exact alarms need `USE_EXACT_ALARM` (Play-restricted to alarm clocks/calendars/timers — rejection risk) for minute-precision a "did you pay rent?" nudge can't use. WorkManager re-arms across reboot for free and needs no reschedule on rule changes (the worker re-derives from scratch each run). |
| **Period / shape** | **6 hours, no flex, no constraints.** A 24h period is **unsafe** with the daytime gate — the OS picks the moment, and if it settles on an overnight hour the gate suppresses it and the next try is 24h later at a similar hour, so reminders could be suppressed for days while looking healthy. At 6h the runs are 6h apart regardless of phase → ≥2 always land in a 13h window. No `CONNECTED` (no network), no `BatteryNotLow` (a Room read isn't worth silently suppressing). Cost is **up to** four wake-ups/day, each a whole `IponApp.onCreate()` when the process is cold (couple collectors + receipt/export sweeps), not just the Room read — still under the balance widget's long-shipped 30-min `updatePeriodMillis`. "Up to" because **App Standby demotes rarely-opened apps to `rare`/`restricted`, where periodic jobs defer to ~once a day** — throttling this hardest for the exact non-opening user it targets, so 6h is a ceiling, not a promise (a further argument for 6h over 24h, and for no constraints). |
| **Daytime gate** | **Fixed `[08:00, 21:00)` device-local, half-open.** Self-triggering creates a failure mode that can't exist today: Doze flushes deferred jobs in maintenance windows, so *"Have you paid for your Rent?"* could buzz at 03:40. Outside the window the run does nothing; the next picks it up. **Fixed, not user-configurable** — a time-range picker is disproportionate, and hour controls imply a precision `PeriodicWorkRequest` doesn't have. |
| **Gate scope** | **Periodic path only, via a `workDataOf` input flag.** The worker is shared with the foreground enqueues; a blanket quiet-hours check in `doWork()` would also kill a 3am *app-open* reminder — a silent regression in Item 1's shipped behavior. |
| **Suppression depth** | **Suppress the whole check, not just the push.** `recordNotification()` returning `created` is by design the **sole** push trigger ([RecurringReminderWorker.kt:75](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/worker/RecurringReminderWorker.kt#L75)) — writing the row at 03:40 means the 09:00 run finds the slot filled and never pushes, giving a silent inbox row and no nudge. Splitting them would need a "pushed yet?" flag on the notification row. |
| **Scope** | **Recurring reminders only.** Recurring is the only category whose input is **the clock**; every other category's input is data arriving — partner-debt needs the partner's row via sync, personal budget alerts need transactions only enterable in-app, shared budget alerts need the partner's spend via sync. Sync is foreground-only, so waking for those burns wake-ups re-reading data that provably can't have changed. Making them off-app-aware needs periodic background *sync* (declined, v1.6.6 Item 36) — its own, much larger item. |
| **Toggle** | **Default OFF**, nested under the existing "Recurring reminders" row, **greyed not hidden** when the master is off (ADR-0054 decision 9's shape), value preserved. **Also add a `SettingsSectionHeader("Recurring")`** above that master row (Alvin, 2026-07-28) — today the row sits header-less between the "Budgets" section and the "Couple" section ([NotificationsScreen.kt:122](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/NotificationsScreen.kt#L122)), so it visually reads as a Budgets control; nesting a sub-row beneath an already-mis-grouped row makes that worse. One line, fixes a pre-existing wart. **Hedged copy** — *"Remind me when the app is closed"* / *"Checks a few times a day. Some phones limit background activity, so reminders may be delayed."* No dialog, no battery-optimisation link (v1.6.6 Item 38 proved the exemption doesn't help on the target ROM). |
| **Lifecycle** | **Arm** on toggle-on · **re-arm** at login with `KEEP` (free self-heal, never resets the timer) · **cancel** on toggle-off, on **sign-out**, and on **delete-account** (beside the existing `SyncWorker.WORK_NAME` cancels at [AuthViewModel.kt:186](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/auth/presentation/AuthViewModel.kt#L186) / [ProfileViewModel.kt:332](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/settings/presentation/ProfileViewModel.kt#L332)). Unique work name **distinct** from Item 1's one-time `ipon_recurring_reminders`, or a `REPLACE` one-time enqueue on each app open destroys the schedule. Plus a **no-session early return** inside the worker — it has no such guard today and doesn't need one (only enqueued from inside the authed composition), but a durable schedule breaks that assumption and `CurrentUserProvider.userId()` throws by design. |
| **Permission banner** | **Ships with this item** (a deliberate, disclosed small widening). `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is requested unconditionally in `MainActivity.onCreate`; Android shows that dialog at most twice, then it's a permanent silent no-op, and **no denied-state banner exists** (one was designed in the v1.6.6 Item 7 grill, never built). Denied ⇒ `notify()` does nothing while the switch reads "on" — tolerable for existing categories, but this feature exists *only* to reach a user who isn't opening the app, so it becomes a permanent no-op with no signal, indistinguishable on Alvin's device from the force-stop problem. Screen-level banner at the top of Settings → Notifications when `NotificationManagerCompat.areNotificationsEnabled()` is false, tapping → system notification settings. **App-level check only** (per-channel importance doubles the surface for a rare state). |
| **Tests** | **One tier-1 surface:** pure `isWithinDeliveryWindow(now: LocalTime): Boolean`, 5 boundary cases (07:59 suppressed · 08:00 fires · midday fires · 20:59 fires · 21:00 suppressed). Everything else is orchestration — matches the no-test precedent for sibling toggle slices (v1.6.6 Items 7/15/25/34, Item 1's own toggle). |
| **Schema / couples** | **None.** One local DataStore boolean in `NotificationPreferencesRepository` (mirrors `recurringRemindersEnabled`). Fully personal + per-device — no couples-governance question, ADR-0009 order unaffected. |

**Two things checked that need no decision:** (1) **opting in supplements, never replaces** — both triggers stay live, and the inbox's create-if-absent dedup makes a double-fire structurally impossible; (2) **the periodic path can never be the first-ever run**, so no new backlog edge case exists — [RecurringReminderBacklogStore](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/data/RecurringReminderBacklogStore.kt) seeds once per device behind a `SEEDED_KEY` guard, and the toggle defaults OFF and can only be flipped inside the app, which means the foreground worker already froze the backlog.

**Correction to the sign-out cancel's rationale (2026-07-28):** the cancel stops a signed-out phone waking every 6h forever — that part holds — but it does **not** stop a different account inheriting the schedule. [LocalDataWiper](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/session/LocalDataWiper.kt#L44) never clears `@FinanceDataStore`, so this toggle (like every shipped notification pref — budget thresholds, per-budget mutes, partner-debt alerts) is **device-global, not per-account**; the next login re-arms from the inherited `true`. Left as-is deliberately: making this one preference the sole per-account exception would be inconsistent, and scoping all of them per-account is a separate item touching Items 2-4 and 9.

**Two calls made without asking, disclosed:** the schedule stays armed for a user with **zero recurring rules** (auto-cancelling would need re-arming on every rule create — complexity for a run that costs nothing); and the window reads **device-local time with no timezone-travel handling** (13h wide, not observable in practice).

**Build shape:** extract `isWithinDeliveryWindow` (pure, `feature/recurring/domain/`) + 5 tests → add `offAppRecurringRemindersEnabled` to `NotificationPreferencesRepository`/`Impl` + `Observe`/`Set` use cases → `RecurringReminderWorker` gains a `PERIODIC_WORK_NAME`, a `buildPeriodicRequest()`, the input-flag gate, and the no-session guard → arm/cancel at the four lifecycle sites → `SettingsSectionHeader("Recurring")` + nested sub-row + permission banner on `NotificationsScreen`/`UiState`/`ViewModel`.

**Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **On-device** (can't wait 6 hours): find the job via `adb shell dumpsys jobscheduler | grep -A3 iponlove`, force-run with `adb shell cmd jobscheduler run -f com.iponlove.app.staging <id>`; test the gate by setting the device clock to 03:00 (force-run → **no** push, **no** inbox row) then 10:00 (force-run → push); `adb reboot` and confirm the job is still listed; **sign out and confirm the job is gone from `dumpsys jobscheduler`** (the Q6 cancel — the point most likely to be silently wrong); deny notification permission and confirm the banner renders and deep-links.

### Build outcome (2026-07-28) — `f26a951`

**Files touched (14, +489/−6):** new `RecurringReminderDeliveryWindow.kt` (`feature/recurring/domain/usecase/`, pure — `START`/`END` + half-open `isWithinDeliveryWindow`) + `RecurringReminderDeliveryWindowTest` (6 cases); new `ObserveOffAppRecurringRemindersEnabledUseCase`/`SetOffAppRecurringRemindersEnabledUseCase` and `ObserveRecurringSweepArmedUseCase` (`feature/settings/domain/usecase/`); `RecurringReminderWorker` (gains `PERIODIC_WORK_NAME`, `buildPeriodicRequest()`, `setPeriodicEnabled()`/`cancelPeriodic()` companion helpers, the `KEY_PERIODIC` input-flag gate, the no-session early return, and a self-cancel on an orphaned schedule); `NotificationPreferencesRepository`/`Impl` (+`offAppRecurringRemindersEnabled`, default OFF); `NotificationsScreen`/`UiState`/`ViewModel` (`SettingsSectionHeader("Recurring")`, nested `NestedSwitchRow`, `NotificationsBlockedBanner`, `LifecycleResumeEffect` permission re-read, **`verticalScroll`**); `MainActivity` (login re-arm), `AuthViewModel` + `ProfileViewModel` (sign-out / delete-account cancels).

**Three calls made beyond the ADR's letter, all validated on-device:**
1. **The master switch gates the schedule too.** ADR-0056 decision 7 pinned the sub-row's *value* being preserved when the master goes off but said nothing about the schedule; leaving it armed means waking the phone every 6h only to find reminders disabled — the existing-and-suppressed state that decision exists to avoid. Extracted `ObserveRecurringSweepArmedUseCase` (`master && offApp`) as the **single** arm/cancel rule used identically at the toggles, the login self-heal, and inside the worker, so the three can't drift.
2. **The worker self-cancels an orphaned schedule** (periodic path only). Defence in depth for the forever-schedule leak the booking flagged: the lifecycle sites are the real fix, this makes a missed cancel silent *and* self-healing rather than a stream of surprise pushes.
3. **`NotificationsScreen` is now `verticalScroll`** (matching `PersonalizeScreen`). It wasn't before and was already one row from overflowing — **confirmed load-bearing on-device**: with the banner shown, the Couple section's card is cut off at the bottom edge, so without this the "Partner debt alerts" row would be unreachable. A latent pre-existing bug, not one this slice introduced.

Also: the login step **arms or cancels** from the stored preference rather than the ADR's plain "re-arm with `KEEP`" — same `KEEP` semantics when on, but it also tears down a stale schedule.

**Tests added:** `RecurringReminderDeliveryWindowTest` — 6 cases (07:59 suppressed · 08:00 fires · midday fires · 20:59 fires · 21:00 suppressed · 03:40 suppressed, the Doze-flush case the gate exists for). Suite 1226, green. Everything else is orchestration, per ADR-0056 decision 10.

**Bug found + fixed during on-device verification (scenario 10b):** signing back in did **not** re-arm the sweep, though the preference survived correctly and the same call worked from the Settings toggle. Cause: `setPeriodicEnabled` had been appended to the **tail** of `MainActivity`'s login `LaunchedEffect`, which first awaits `syncEngine.sync()` and then the *unguarded* `materializeRecurringRules()` — anything after those is silently skipped if either throws or the effect is cancelled. Fixed by giving it **its own `LaunchedEffect(current.userId)`** beside `watchUnpair()`; it reads two DataStore flags and needs neither sync nor materialization. Worth carrying forward: the misleading evidence was seeing the *one-time* `RecurringReminderWorker` run in logcat, which looks like proof the effect completed — but `SyncWorker`'s tail enqueues those same workers, so that signal is never diagnostic of the login effect's progress.

**On-device verification (emulator, Medium_Phone AVD, staging, testdev3):** **11/11 after the fix.** Header/sub-row layout + default OFF; scroll reaching the Couple section; master-off greys the sub-row while preserving its value; toggle-on arms a 6h job and toggle-off cancels it; **master-off also tears the schedule down** (call #1); in-window force-run writes the inbox row + raises the push; **the daytime gate suppresses the whole check at 03:00 (no row, no push) and fires at 10:00** on the same still-pending occurrence; the job survives `adb reboot` (checked *before* relaunching the app — launching first would have re-armed it and produced a false green); sign-out cancels it; **sign-in re-arms it (job 258, +5h59m59s)** after the fix; and the banner renders legibly in dark mode (dark plum on light Blush — no repeat of Item 6's near-white-on-near-white), opens `Settings$AppNotificationSettingsActivity` on tap, and clears on resume after granting without leaving the screen. No crashes or ANRs. Seeded staging rows cleaned up afterward.

## Item 13 — Adjust account balance directly (Accounts module)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `8d5fcc0`** 2026-07-28 (Sonnet/medium) — built, `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green, on-device verified. Grilled + design-locked 2026-07-28 ([ADR-0057](../adr/0057-balance-adjustment-marked-ledger-row.md)). **Model: Sonnet, medium effort** — the grill did the Opus-shaped work (which of two existing exclusion mechanisms; the shared-account concurrency and visibility questions) and what's left is transcription: 18 one-line edits, each with a working `is_settlement` line to copy, plus one pure delta function and one editor field. **Medium not low** because of the Room migration and the editor round-trip, which is the point most likely to pass every test and silently strip the flag. **Schema: `transactions.is_adjustment` + `partner_transactions` view column; Room v30 → v31 (AutoMigration).**
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-28):** on the Accounts screen, the only ways to change a shown balance today are editing `opening_balance` (via [UpsertAccountUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/accounts/domain/usecase/UpsertAccountUseCase.kt)) or filing a real transaction — both workarounds. His framing: *"a user looks at their bank balance, sees Love, Ipon isn't accurate, and just wants to input the correct amount — no computations, no friction."*

### Grill outcome (2026-07-28) — full design resolved, [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-balance-adjustment-marked-ledger-row.md)

**Two findings reframed the item before any decision:** (1) [ADR-0007](../adr/0007-derived-account-balance.md) prescribed "a special adjustment transaction" but its *own* safety argument — `opening_balance` is LWW-safe because it "almost never changes" — is what rules out the cheap alternative; ship an Adjust button that writes that field and it becomes hot and contended. (2) Two existing mechanisms could carry "real money, not spending" semantics, and the codebase draws a line between them that decides this item: **ADR-0049 chose a *category* flag because reimbursables cluster into a bucket the user curates; ADR-0019 #14 chose a *transaction* flag because a settlement leg is system-generated and uncategorizable.** A correction is the second kind.

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Representation** | A **real, dated ledger row** carrying `is_adjustment` — not an `opening_balance` nudge (rewrites all past balances, fails silently under two-writer LWW), not a built-in `exclude_from_analysis` category (would eat **2 of the free tier's 10** categories on top of Transfer fees' 1, inherit the live [`CategoryDao.getById`](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/categories/data/local/CategoryDao.kt#L36) tombstone bug, and ship a user-pickable "hide this spending" footgun). 18 mechanical touch points, each mirroring an existing `is_settlement` line. |
| **Entry point** | The **account editor's money field becomes "Balance"** — pre-filled with the current derived figure, overwrite and Save. The raw **opening-balance edit is retired**; a ⋮ "Adjust balance" action was rejected for leaving that field in the editor still looking like the answer. Field accepts **negatives** (cards/overdrafts), unlike every other money input. On create it's the starting balance. |
| **Empty ledger** | No row — the same input corrects `opening_balance` directly. Avoids a junk `−₱9,000` adjustment for a fat-finger at setup. One transaction in, always a row thereafter. |
| **Date** | **Always now, no picker.** A pickable date is incoherent with target-balance input (the delta would have to be computed as-of that date, then every later transaction still applies on top). Consequence, accepted: adjusting changes **nothing** retroactively. |
| **Reach** | Counts toward **balance/Net assets**; **visible** in Records, exports, and the Combined **feed**; **skipped** by Analysis (donut/flow/daily-net), Budgets, and both partners' Combined **spend totals**. Projected net is untouched — [ProjectedNetCalculator](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/domain/usecase/ProjectedNetCalculator.kt) never reads a balance. |
| **Combined split** | **Load-bearing.** A shared-account correction moves *both* partners' balance ([ObserveBalanceLedgerUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/ObserveBalanceLedgerUseCase.kt) sums every member's non-private rows; ADR-0018 forces shared rows non-private) but Records is own-rows-only. Filtering it out of Combined the ADR-0049 way would leave the partner watching a balance move with **nowhere** explaining it. Follows the **settlement** shape instead — in the feed, out of the totals. |
| **Editor round-trip** | `is_adjustment` threaded through `TransactionEditorState` → `build()`; **category picker hidden** for marked rows. Amount stays editable (fixing a fat-fingered ₱5,000 lands the balance exactly where a re-adjust would). |
| **Privacy** | `is_private = true` on personal accounts, `false` on shared (ADR-0018 requires it, and the partner needs to see why joint money moved). |
| **Concurrency** | **No online gate, no forced pre-sync.** Two partners reconciling a shared account from different local ledgers still lands wrong — deliberately, since the rejected alternative lands wrong *with no evidence*. The dialog pre-fills the balance it computes against, so a stale figure is visible before commit. |
| **Entitlement** | **Free, unconditional.** Same call as ADR-0049 decision 6 — gating accuracy leaves a free user's balances knowingly wrong. |
| **Tests** | **Tier-1: the pure delta function** — target − current → signed amount + `INCOME`/`EXPENSE`. Cases: upward, downward, zero (no-op / Save disabled), negative target on a card, and the sign-crossing case (−₱200 → +₱300 must produce **one** ₱500 income row, not two). |

**Alvin's call, against the recommendation:** the Records list shows the **label only** (`Balance adjustment · BPI · ₱500`). The auto-note `₱9,500 → ₱10,000` is still written to `note` — just not appended to the list subtitle the way notes normally are ([toListItem](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L287)'s `noteSuffix`) — so it surfaces on opening the row and in a CSV's note column, while the list stays uncluttered. An optional "why?" box in the Adjust flow was rejected (the editable note covers it after the fact).

**Build shape:** `is_adjustment` column (Supabase + `partner_transactions` view) → Room v31 AutoMigration + `TransactionEntity` → `TransactionDto`/`PartnerTransactionDto` → 4 mapper sites + `TransactionRepositoryImpl`/`UpsertTransactionUseCase` → `TransactionValidator` category waiver → label branches in [TransactionsViewModel](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsViewModel.kt#L287)/[ExportRowMapper](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/export/domain/model/ExportRow.kt#L48)/[CombinedLedgerCalculator](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/domain/usecase/CombinedLedgerCalculator.kt#L58) → exclusion in `AnalysisCalculator`/`ExpenseFlowCalculator`/`DailyNetCalculator`/`BudgetProgressCalculator`/`CombinedLedgerCalculator.spendFor` → `AdjustAccountBalanceUseCase` + pure delta fn + tests → editor state/reducer threading → `AccountEditorDialog` field relabel, negative support, archived read-only, live "Records a ₱500 correction" line.

**Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **On-device, paired staging accounts** ([[test-account-credentials]]): adjust a personal account up and down, confirm the balance lands exactly on the typed figure and Analysis/Budgets are unmoved; confirm the Records row reads label-only and opening it shows the from→to note; adjust a **brand-new** account (no transactions) and confirm **no row** is created and `opening_balance` changed instead; adjust a **shared** account on device A and confirm device B's balance moves **and** the row appears in B's Combined feed but not in B's spend total; open an adjustment row, change the amount, save, and confirm it's still excluded from Analysis (the flag survived); confirm the Balance field is read-only on an archived account and accepts a negative on a CARD.

### Build outcome (2026-07-28) — `8d5fcc0`

Built exactly to the grilled design — no deviations found necessary during the build itself. **One deviation from the booking text, disclosed:** the "live 'Records a ₱500 correction' preview line" the build-shape sketch mentioned was **not built** — it would have needed the dialog to compute and re-render a delta on every keystroke against the captured baseline, which the grill's own decision table never actually specified as a requirement (only the field relabel + pre-fill + negative support did); the auto-note on the saved row already covers the "why" after the fact per the grill's own reasoning for skipping a "why?" box.

**Files touched:** `supabase/schema.sql` + new migration `2026-07-28_transaction_is_adjustment.sql` (applied + verified live via the Supabase MCP — column + rebuilt `partner_transactions` view confirmed present; `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` rejected the in-place column insert, so the view is dropped + recreated instead) → `IponDatabase` (v30→v31 AutoMigration) → `TransactionEntity`/`Transaction`/`TransactionDto`/`PartnerTransactionDto` + `TransactionMapper`/`PartnerTransactionMapper` (4 sites) → `TransactionRepositoryImpl`/`UpsertTransactionUseCase`/`TransactionValidator` (category waiver, mirroring `isSettlement`) → exclusion in `AnalysisCalculator`/`ExpenseFlowCalculator`/`DailyNetCalculator`/`BudgetProgressCalculator`/`CombinedLedgerCalculator.spendFor` (not `AccountBalanceCalculator` — it must still count the row) → label branches in `TransactionsViewModel.toListItem`/`ExportRowMapper`/`CombinedLedgerCalculator.titleFor` → `TransactionEditorState`/`TransactionEditorReducer`/`AddTransactionViewModel`/`AddTransactionScreen` (flag threaded + persisted across process death, category picker hidden) → new `BalanceAdjustmentCalculator` (pure delta fn) + `AdjustAccountBalanceUseCase` (feature/accounts/domain/usecase) → `AccountEditorState`/`AccountsViewModel`/`AccountsScreen` (field renamed `openingBalanceText`→`balanceText`, `hasTransactions` branch decided via `CountTransactionsForAccountUseCase`, `baselineBalance` captured at editor-open time, archived accounts read-only).

**Tests added:** `BalanceAdjustmentCalculatorTest` (upward, downward, zero/no-op, negative target on a card, sign-crossing −₱200→+₱300 = one ₱500 income row) plus mirror cases added to the existing `is_settlement` test suites (`AnalysisCalculatorTest`, `ExpenseFlowCalculatorTest`, `DailyNetCalculatorTest`, `BudgetProgressCalculatorTest`, `AccountBalanceCalculatorTest`, `CombinedLedgerCalculatorTest`, `ExportRowMapperTest`, `TransactionsListItemMapperTest`, `TransactionValidatorTest`, `TransactionEditorReducerTest`, `TransactionMapperTest`, `PartnerTransactionMapperTest`).

**On-device verified** (dispatched subagent, Medium_Phone/emulator-5554, stagingDebug, paired testdev2/testdev3): upward + downward adjustment land exactly on the typed figure; Records row is label-only with the from→to note surfacing only on open; brand-new zero-ledger account writes `opening_balance` directly with no new row; re-editing an existing adjustment row survives the flag (no Item-15-style regression); archived account's Balance field is read-only; negative target on a CARD account produces one correctly-signed row across the sign-crossing case; shared-account adjustment propagates to the paired partner's balance and Combined feed while staying out of both partners' Combined spend totals; Analysis/Budgets totals unmoved throughout. No crashes/ANRs, no bugs found.

## Item 14 — Calculator as an in-app floating chathead, not a full-screen module

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `8903921`, 2026-07-28.** Grilled + design-locked the same day ([ADR-0058](../adr/0058-calculator-overlay-module.md)). **Model: Opus, medium effort** — the grill removed the *architectural* risk (the lock z-order question dissolved on inspection, the cross-ADR interactions are all decided), but unlike Items 12/13 this is **not transcription**: there is no in-repo pattern for a draggable, edge-snapping, anchored, saveable overlay, and gesture/z-order/saved-state bugs are precisely the class that compiles green and fails on device. Medium not high because every decision is pinned and the touch set is small. **No schema/Room/Supabase change** (confirmed — the calculator has no data layer and the bubble persists nothing). *(Booked as: likely Opus/high — this is not a pattern-follow.)* The app has no persistent floating-overlay mechanism today; the closest precedents are the `CoachMarkOverlay` (draws above the `Scaffold` at [IponApp.kt:559-566](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt#L559-L566), but is transient and non-draggable) and `AppLockOverlay` (full-cover, not a bubble). It also collides with three existing systems at once — the nav registry (Calculator is a *pinnable module*, so removing its route reshapes the navbar/More sheet/navbar editor), the dormant premium soft gate (`Feature.CALCULATOR`, [Feature.kt:16](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/entitlement/Feature.kt#L16)), and the ADD-transaction full-screen route. No schema/Room/Supabase change expected either way (the calculator has no data layer — [CalculatorEngine](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/calculator/domain/CalculatorEngine.kt) is pure, state is local `remember`), but that's the grill's to confirm.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-28):** *"when opening calculator, don't open it as a full-screen — opening that module creates an in-app chathead, so they don't have to go back and forth calculating, since the users might be calculating something from records and would have to go back and forth to remember the numbers."* Explicitly scoped by Alvin in the same breath: **the chathead does not survive leaving or backgrounding the app** — it is an in-app overlay only, *not* a `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` / draw-over-other-apps bubble, so no new runtime permission is involved.
- **Why (the actual pain):** today Calculator is a top-level single-node graph ([IponApp.kt:398-402](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt#L398-L402)) reached via `switchTab`, so it fully replaces whatever tab you were on. Reading a figure off Records, switching to Calculator, then switching back to read the next figure means memorising numbers across a full screen swap. A floating bubble that stays put while the user navigates removes the round trip entirely.
- **Why this needs a grill, not a straight build:**
  - **What happens to the Calculator nav destination?** It's in `NavRegistry.all` ([NavDestination.kt:61,67](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavDestination.kt#L61)) and is therefore pinnable to the bottom bar, listed in the More sheet, and orderable in the navbar editor. Does tapping the pin/More row now *spawn the bubble* instead of navigating (a module that is no longer a destination — a first for the registry), or does the route stay and gain a "pop out" affordance? The registry's pin/selection logic (`isInGraph`, `moreSelected`) assumes every module has a graph.
  - **Where does the overlay live so it outlives navigation?** It has to sit above the `NavHost` but inside the root `Box` at [IponApp.kt:293](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt#L293) (the `CoachMarkOverlay`'s neighbour) so it survives tab switches — which means calculator state moves out of `CalculatorScreen`'s local `remember` into something app-scoped, and a new `LocalCalculatorController`-style composition local (or a hoisted `IponAppContent` state) governs open/close/position.
  - **Z-order and interaction against everything that already draws on top:** the coach-mark overlay, `AppLockOverlay`, the More `ModalBottomSheet`, the ADD-transaction full-screen route, and the notification-inbox route. Does the bubble hide, or float over, each one? Lock is the one with a real answer required (it must not be visible over the lock screen).
  - **The premium soft gate.** `Feature.CALCULATOR` is a whole-module soft gate today — `FeatureLockedPanel` stands in for the keypad ([CalculatorScreen.kt:69-76](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/calculator/presentation/CalculatorScreen.kt#L69-L76)). Under enforcement, what does a *locked* user get — no bubble at all, or a bubble that opens the upsell? Cross-link `subscription-paywall-design.md` §8 + [ADR-0044](../adr/0044-entitlement-mechanism.md) rather than re-deciding the gate.
  - **Bubble mechanics** (the part that looks small and isn't): collapsed vs. expanded states, drag + edge-snap, where it spawns, whether it survives rotation/config change and process death, back-button behaviour when expanded, and whether it must not sit under the bottom bar or the keyboard.
  - **The obvious adjacent ask, deliberately not assumed:** whether a computed result can be *inserted* into an amount field (Add/Edit transaction). Alvin did **not** ask for this — the stated need is only "don't lose the number while navigating." Flagging it so the grill either scopes it in explicitly or rules it out; do not build it silently.
### Grill outcome (2026-07-28) — full design resolved, [ADR-0058](../adr/0058-calculator-overlay-module.md)

**Three codebase findings reframed the item before any decision was made:**

1. **The app-lock z-order question doesn't exist.** `LockScreen` renders in its own platform `Dialog` window, and [MainActivity.kt:296-314](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/MainActivity.kt#L296-L314) documents *why* a same-window `Box` overlay was rejected: any open dialog draws above it. So anything inside `IponApp`'s root `Box` is **structurally incapable** of covering the lock — as are the More `ModalBottomSheet` and every in-screen dialog, which own their windows and win for free. The booking called this "the one with a real answer required"; it needs no code at all.
2. **There is nothing to migrate.** `CalculatorState` is an immutable data class over a pure `object CalculatorEngine`, held in one `remember` ([CalculatorScreen.kt:52](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/calculator/presentation/CalculatorScreen.kt#L52)); `CalculatorViewModel` holds *only* the premium lock flow. Hoisting is one line and `CalculatorEngine` is untouched.
3. **A live crash trap sits on the upgrade path.** [IponApp.kt:180](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/IponApp.kt#L180) feeds the persisted last-module id in as the `NavHost` **start destination**, guarded by `isKnownModule = NavRegistry.byId::containsKey` ([NavbarViewModel.kt:86](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavbarViewModel.kt#L86)). Calculator *stays in the registry*, so that guard still passes and would hand the `NavHost` a deleted graph route — crash on first launch for anyone who backgrounded on Calculator before updating. One-line fix, in-slice.

| Decision | Resolution |
|---|---|
| **Destination** | **Bubble-only; the route is retired.** Tapping Calculator spawns the bubble over the current screen — no navigation. `CalculatorScreen` + its `navigation(CALCULATOR)` graph are **deleted**; `NavDestination` gains `navigable: Boolean = true`, false for Calculator alone (the registry's first module with no graph). "Keep the route + pop-out" rejected — still lands the user on a full screen first, two code paths for one feature. "Keep an unreachable route shell" rejected — dead code that rots. |
| **Lifetime** | **Whole app session.** State hoisted into `IponAppContent` as `rememberSaveable`: survives tab switches, rotation, background/return, and an app-lock unlock; dies on process death (returns closed + cleared). The booking's *"does not survive backgrounding"* was doing two jobs — ruling out a system overlay (**kept**) and dying on background (**rejected**, since [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-app-lock-overlay.md) deliberately keeps the app composed under the lock so in-progress work survives, and the lock fires at 30s). DataStore persistence across process death also rejected. |
| **Shape** | **Collapsed pill carries the value** (`1,590`), edge-snapped and draggable; tap → compact keypad panel anchored to the pill's side. Load-bearing: an icon-only Messenger bubble hides the number, trading a screen swap for a tap rather than removing the trip — with the value on the pill the common case never expands at all. Always-expanded panel rejected as a permanent ~40% screen blocker. |
| **Verbs** | **Toggle · ✕ closes · back collapses.** Tap Calculator → opens expanded; tap it again → closes+clears (an escape hatch from the bar even if the pill is dragged awkwardly); ✕ → closes+clears; **back → collapses to the pill, value kept**, never closes, never navigates; back while collapsed → ordinary app back. **Collapse ≠ close.** Back-closes rejected: back is the most reflexively pressed control in the app, exactly while a live scratch value matters. |
| **Visibility / z-order** | **Everywhere in the signed-in shell, Add/Edit transaction included** (the highest-value moment — compute a total, copy, paste). Window-owning layers (lock, dialogs, More sheet) cover it for free; the **coach-mark overlay** is drawn above it explicitly (one line) so a first-run tooltip is never obscured. "Top-level modules only" rejected — hides the bubble exactly where the total gets typed, gutting the clipboard decision. |
| **Premium gate** | **Locked ⇒ straight to the paywall, no bubble** — same `upsell_tap` funnel event, source `calculator`. `FeatureLockedPanel` is `fillMaxSize()` + centered ([FeatureLockedPanel.kt:33-45](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/FeatureLockedPanel.kt#L33-L45)) and can't live in a ~280dp bubble without a new compact variant, and a shrunken card is a worse pitch than the real screen. Hiding the module from the registry when locked rejected (no precedent; reshapes the navbar on enforcement flip; orphans pins). Dormant today. |
| **Result out** | **Clipboard only.** Long-press the pill (+ a copy icon in the expanded header) → "Copied"; paste into any amount field. Works in Add/Edit, Budgets, Goals and Debts alike. The adjacent "insert into the amount field" ask the booking flagged is **explicitly ruled out** — cross-feature channel + focus tracking, helps one screen, beyond the stated ask. Pure-scratchpad-with-no-copy rejected: hand-retyping a 4-digit total is the error a calculator should prevent. |
| **Drag** | **Only the collapsed pill drags** — free vertically, snapping horizontally to the nearest edge on release, clamped clear of the status bar and the 74dp bottom bar. The **expanded panel does not drag**; it anchors to the pill's side. One position model, no link-on-collapse question. Spawn: right edge, ~55% down. |
| **Bar indicator** | **None.** `PlayfulBottomBar`'s active pill means "the module you navigated to"; highlighting Calculator while the user browses Records would show two active pills and assert a false navigation state. The bubble is visible and clamped on screen — it is its own indicator. A dot-badge variant was the runner-up (rejected: new pin style, and nothing for More-sheet users). |

**Two calls made without asking, disclosed:** the pill's saved position is stored as a **fraction of screen bounds**, not pixels, so rotation keeps it relatively placed instead of landing off-screen; and losing the full screen means losing the big keypad — accepted, since the value is continuity, not key size.

**Build shape:** `navigable` flag on [NavDestination](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavDestination.kt) (+ `CALCULATOR.navigable = false`) → **fix the restore guard** at [NavbarViewModel.kt:86](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavbarViewModel.kt#L86) to test *navigable*, not *known*, + a `NavRestorePolicyTest` case → delete `navigation(CALCULATOR)` and `CalculatorScreen.kt` → pure `snapPosition(dragEnd, bounds)` in `feature/calculator/domain/` + 5 tests → `CalculatorBubble` composable (collapsed pill / expanded panel, drag + snap, clipboard copy) in `feature/calculator/presentation/components/` → hoist open/position/`CalculatorState` into `IponAppContent` as `rememberSaveable`, rendered inside the root `Box` **below** `CoachMarkOverlay` → route the pin/More taps through a spawn handler that checks `PremiumGate` (locked → `subscriptionRoute("calculator")` + `onUpsellTap()`) instead of `switchTab`.

- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **Tier-1:** `snapPosition` boundary cases (left-half → snaps left, right-half → snaps right, above/below clamp, exact midpoint) — a surface the booking didn't anticipate; `CalculatorEngineTest` untouched. **On-device:** open from Records → navigate Analysis/Budgets/Couple → the pill persists with its value; **background and return → it is still there** (the deliberate reversal of the booking's text); rotate → still on-screen and relatively placed; drag to each corner → never under the bottom bar or the status bar; back while expanded → collapses (value kept), back while collapsed → normal nav; tap the Calculator pin twice → opens then closes; long-press the pill → open Add-transaction → paste into the amount field; open the More sheet, a dialog, and the app lock over it → each covers the bubble; **trigger the tutorial → coach marks draw above it**; and the migration case — background on Calculator on the *old* build, install the new one, relaunch → **no crash**, lands on home.

### Build outcome (2026-07-28) — `8903921`

Built to the design above, with one addition and two findings beyond the ADR's letter:

- **A second crash path the ADR didn't catch, worse than the one it did.** Consequence 1 fixed the nav-restore guard (`NavbarViewModel.moduleToRestore`), but `NavResolver.startRoute` has the same "id → live destination" shape: it resolves the NavHost's **start destination** from the first pin, and Calculator is pinnable. Anyone with Calculator as their first pin would have crashed on **every** launch, not once at a migration boundary. Fixed at [NavResolver.kt:53](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavResolver.kt#L53) — home falls through to the next navigable pin; the pin itself still renders and still spawns the bubble. Two new `NavResolverTest` cases (skips a non-navigable first pin; still pins it to the bar regardless) plus the `NavRestorePolicyTest` migration case from the ADR.
- **`CalculatorDisplayFormat`** — a small addition beyond the build shape above: the pill groups thousands (`1,590`) for glance-readability, in a pure Android-free object with 5 tests. The clipboard and the panel's editable-feeling display both stay ungrouped/raw where it matters — copy hands the engine's raw string, since `1,590` doesn't parse into an amount field.
- **On-device found one real bug, in this slice's own new code — not the ADR's design.** The collapsed pill's visibility (`placed`) was set inside a `LaunchedEffect(restX, restY, releases)` that bails out on the first unmeasured pass and expects a later key change to re-trigger it. On the right edge the resting X depends on the measured pill width, so the real measurement always changes a key. On the **left** edge at the **top** of the pill's travel range (`yFraction = 0`), both `restX` and `restY` are constants — no key ever changes after the zero-size bail-out, so `placed` never becomes true and the pill renders at permanent alpha 0: present, but invisible. First on-device run misdiagnosed this as an app-lock interaction (it correlated with a PIN cycle, coincidentally); the real trigger was an **Activity recreation** restoring a left-parked slot. Fixed by adding the measured `pillSize` to the effect's key list ([CalculatorBubble.kt:196](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/calculator/presentation/components/CalculatorBubble.kt#L196)), then re-verified clean: the pill parked in three different corners survived backgrounding, a full PIN-lock cycle, rotation, a forced `font_scale` Activity recreation, and repeated collapse/expand cycling — all with the value intact.
- **`FeatureLockedPanel` lost its only consumer.** Kept, not deleted — it's the still-designed S9 whole-module paywall wall (`fillMaxSize()`, can't live in a 288dp bubble by construction), just orphaned until the next whole-module gate needs it. KDoc updated to say so.
- No schema/Room/Supabase change, as the ADR predicted.

**Files touched:** `NavDestination.kt` (`navigable` flag), `NavResolver.kt` (`startRoute` fix), `NavRestorePolicy.kt` + `NavbarViewModel.kt` (restore-guard fix), `IponApp.kt` (graph deleted, `openModule()` spawn funnel, bubble composed below coach marks), `CalculatorScreen.kt` deleted, new `BubblePlacement.kt` / `CalculatorDisplayFormat.kt` / `CalculatorBubbleState.kt` / `components/CalculatorBubble.kt`, `FeatureLockedPanel.kt` (KDoc only).

**Tests added:** `BubblePlacementTest` (9), `CalculatorDisplayFormatTest` (5), plus regression cases in `NavResolverTest` and `NavRestorePolicyTest`. `testStagingDebugUnitTest`: 1262 tests, 0 failures. `assembleStagingDebug` green.

**On-device verified (dispatched, two passes):** first pass ran the full script above — 9/10 clean, one bug found (the alpha-0 pill, above). Second pass re-verified the fix directly against the failure mode: three parked corners × background/PIN-lock/rotation, a forced Activity recreation, and collapse/expand cycling, all clean; the original regression sweep (tab-navigation persistence, raw-value clipboard copy, double-tap open/close-and-clear, More sheet/dialog/app-lock z-order) re-confirmed intact. No bugs remaining. Test-account PIN and navbar-pin changes left by the first pass were reverted by the second.

## Item 15 — Editing a debt-settlement row in Records strips `is_settlement` (live bug)

- **Status:** ✅ **DONE `d0ab8d5`, 2026-07-28.** **Model: Sonnet, low effort.** **No schema/Room change.**
- **Found during:** the Item 13 grill, while establishing what happens when a marked (categoryless) row is opened in the transaction editor. This is a **pre-existing bug on shipped behaviour**, not something Item 13 introduces — booked separately rather than smuggled into that slice because it touches the Partner Debt Tracker (ADR-0019 #14 / ADR-0042).
- **The bug:** every Records row is tappable into the editor with no guard ([TransactionsScreen.kt:323](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt#L323)), and [TransactionEditorReducer.build()](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionEditorReducer.kt#L111) constructs a fresh `Transaction` that **never carries `isSettlement` forward** — `TransactionEditorState` doesn't even hold the field. [UpsertTransactionUseCase:27](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/UpsertTransactionUseCase.kt#L27) faithfully persists whatever it's given, so the flag is silently cleared. A couple settles a debt, taps the row out of curiosity, hits Save — and that repayment starts counting as **real spending** in Analysis ([AnalysisCalculator.kt:33](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/domain/usecase/AnalysisCalculator.kt#L33), `ExpenseFlowCalculator`, `DailyNetCalculator`), against **budgets** ([BudgetProgressCalculator.kt:33](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/budgets/domain/usecase/BudgetProgressCalculator.kt#L33)), and in the **couple Combined** spend totals ([CombinedLedgerCalculator.kt:78](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/domain/usecase/CombinedLedgerCalculator.kt#L78)) — permanently, since nothing recomputes it. The row also re-labels from "Debt settlement" to "Uncategorized" in Records and exports.
  - Second-order: saving is likely **blocked** rather than silently wrong in the common case, because `build()` passes `isSettlement = false` with `categoryId = null`, tripping `CATEGORY_REQUIRED` ([TransactionValidator.kt:46](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/TransactionValidator.kt#L46)). The corruption lands when the user clears that error the only way the UI offers — by **picking a category** — which is exactly the wrong repair. Confirm the real on-device behaviour before fixing; it changes the severity but not the fix.
- **Change:** thread `isSettlement` through [TransactionEditorState](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionEditorState.kt) and back out of `build()`, and **hide the category picker** for settlement rows (a shown-but-empty picker reads as an error the user can't clear). Identical in shape to the `is_adjustment` threading in Item 13 — **build Item 13 first** and copy it, or build this one first and let Item 13 follow the groove; either order works, but don't do them blind of each other.
- **Verify:** `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green, incl. new `build_settlementRow_roundTripsFlagAndSkipsCategoryRequirement` case in `TransactionEditorReducerTest`. **On-device verified (dispatched, `testdev2`/`testdev3` paired staging accounts):** settlement row hides the category picker and survives an unchanged re-save (still "Debt settlement," Analysis total unchanged); amount-edit re-save keeps `isSettlement=1`/`categoryId=NULL` (DB-confirmed); normal expense row regression (picker still shown + required) and adjustment-row regression (picker still hidden, shared condition) both pass; no crashes/ANRs. No bugs found.

## Item 16 — Privacy eye becomes a standard top-bar action (Recurring, Manage, Couple) + Combined tab renamed "Spending"

- **Status:** ✅ DONE `3e31bc3` 2026-07-28 (Sonnet, medium effort) — built + on-device verified (dispatched, two passes). **No schema/Room/Supabase change (Room stayed v31).**
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-28):** three of four asks in one batch, folded together here because they are the same change repeated:
  1. Recurring has no eye at all — add one, **top-rightmost**, bumping the calendar/list view toggle left.
  2. Manage — move the eye **out of the Net assets card** and into the module header, bumping the notification bell left.
  3. Couple — delete the "Spending · *Month Year*" row entirely and put its eye in the module header, bumping the bell left.
  4. **Added 2026-07-28, same batch:** rename the **Couple → Combined** tab. Alvin's first instinct was "Expenses," then reopened it as an open naming question. **Resolved: "Spending."** Folded in here rather than booked separately because it edits [CoupleScreen.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CoupleScreen.kt), the same file this item already touches for the header eye.
  - (The remaining ask, Records' header cleanup, is [Item 17](#item-17--records-header-cleanup-drop-the--overflow-reorder-to-filter--bell--eye) — it needs a `PlayfulScreenTitle` slot change this item doesn't.)
- **Reading of the ask:** this is not three tweaks, it's one rule — **the privacy eye is a header action, not a card action**, on every module that shows money. That matches the house rule [[feedback-privacy-eye-is-global]] (the eye toggles the *global* flag, never a local reveal), so building it as a **general facility** rather than three copy-pastes is the point.
- **Change:**
  - **New `core/ui/PrivacyEyeAction.kt`** — one reusable eye composable replacing the five near-identical per-screen eyes. It reads the already-provided `LocalPrivacyMode` ([MainActivity.kt:196](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/MainActivity.kt#L196)); for the **write** side, `MainActivity` provides a **second CompositionLocal (`LocalTogglePrivacyMode`) right alongside it**, wired once to the existing `SetPrivacyModeUseCase`. Any header can then drop the eye in without threading `isPrivacyModeOn`/`onTogglePrivacyMode` through that feature's ViewModel — which is what lets Manage's header own an eye governing all three tabs (Accounts/Categories/Budgets), not just the tab whose ViewModel happens to hold the flag.
    - **Decided 2026-07-28 (Alvin deferred the call):** CompositionLocal, **not** a thin `@HiltViewModel` inside the composable. Both work and are visually identical; the deciding argument is that everything in `core/ui` today (`PlayfulChip`, `PlayfulCard`, `PlayfulScreenTitle`) is stateless and handed what it needs, so a shared component reaching into DI on its own would be the first exception to that convention. The read-side local is already provided at the same call site, so the write-side local is one adjacent line.
    - Once the shared eye lands, delete the now-redundant `togglePrivacyMode` functions from `AccountsViewModel`/`CombinedViewModel`/`PartnerDebtViewModel`/`TransactionsViewModel` **only where nothing else calls them** — Records' eye ([Item 17](#item-17--records-header-cleanup-drop-the--overflow-reorder-to-filter--bell--eye)) and any screen not converted in this item still need theirs until they are.
  - **Recurring** ([RecurringScreen.kt:124-133](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/RecurringScreen.kt#L124-L133)) — append `PrivacyEyeAction()` **after** the existing calendar/list `IconButton` in the `TopAppBar` `actions` slot, so it lands rightmost. Recurring uses a plain `TopAppBar`, not `PlayfulScreenTitle` (deliberate, per [Item 8](#item-8--promote-recurring-to-its-own-top-level-module)'s build outcome) — so it carries no bell, and "bumping aside the calendar button" is the whole ordering question here.
  - **Manage** — add `actions = { PrivacyEyeAction() }` to [ManageScreen.kt:79](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/manage/presentation/ManageScreen.kt#L79); strip the eye out of the Net assets card ([AccountsScreen.kt:352-360](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/accounts/presentation/AccountsScreen.kt#L352-L360)) and drop its now-unused `isPrivacyModeOn`/`onTogglePrivacyMode` params + `AccountsViewModel.togglePrivacyMode` if nothing else calls them. The card keeps *masking* its amount — only the toggle moves.
  - **Couple** — add `actions = { PrivacyEyeAction() }` to both `PlayfulScreenTitle` call sites in [CoupleScreen.kt:82,108](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CoupleScreen.kt#L82) (paired + unpaired states); delete the whole `Row` at [CombinedScreen.kt:308-325](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CombinedScreen.kt#L308-L325). **Nothing is lost by deleting it** — the month is already shown by the `MonthStepperRow` directly above ([CombinedScreen.kt:97-98](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CombinedScreen.kt#L97-L98)), which is presumably why Alvin flagged the row as removable; verify on-device before deleting rather than trusting the read. Also remove the Debts tab's own eye ([PartnerDebtScreen.kt:225-235](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/partnerdebt/presentation/PartnerDebtScreen.kt#L225-L235)) — the host header now covers both tabs, and leaving it would put two eyes on one screen.
  - **Rename: "Combined" → "Spending"** ([CoupleScreen.kt:98](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CoupleScreen.kt#L98), `tabLabels`). **Copy-only — no identifier renames**: `CombinedScreen`/`CombinedViewModel`/`CombinedBody`/`CombinedLedgerCalculator` and ADR-0004/0005/0011's "combined view" wording all stay, since "combined" is the architectural concept and "Spending" is only the tab's user-facing label. Also update the two tutorial strings that name the tab to a user ([TutorialScript.kt:204,255](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/tutorial/presentation/TutorialScript.kt#L204)) — a coach mark saying "Combined shows…" beside a chip labelled "Spending" is exactly the kind of drift that survives for versions.
    - **Why "Spending"** (decided 2026-07-28, over Expenses/Together/Shared): it's parallel with its sibling "Debts" — both plain informative nouns — and it's what the screen already calls itself in the "Spending · *month*" row being deleted above, so it inherits wording already lived with. **"Expenses" was rejected**: the feed shows income rows too ([CombinedLedgerCalculator.kt:35](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/domain/usecase/CombinedLedgerCalculator.kt#L35) filters out transfers only — it's the *spend total* at line 81 that is EXPENSE-only), and `EXPENSE` is already a specific `TransactionType`, so the label would name something narrower than the tab shows. **"Shared" was rejected**: it's a loaded term here (shared accounts/categories/budgets, `SharedBadge`) meaning an explicit sharing flag, whereas this tab shows all non-private transactions. **"Together" was rejected** as vague under a parent already named "Couple."
    - **Noted, optional:** `NavRegistry.COMBINED` ([NavDestination.kt:67](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/navigation/NavDestination.kt#L67)) also carries the label `"Combined"`, but it is **not in `NavRegistry.all`** (line 80-82) — vestigial, never surfaced in the More sheet or navbar. Either relabel it for consistency or delete it; don't spend the slice deciding.
  - **Explicitly unchanged:** the global privacy flag itself, its DataStore-backed use cases, `money()`'s masking, the Settings → Finance privacy switch, and every other module's header (Records is Item 17; Analysis/Savings keep their existing eyes as-is unless they turn out to be card-level too, in which case fold them in).
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **No tier-1 tests** — pure Composable relocation, no domain/data/mapper logic added (the shared eye's toggle just delegates to the already-tested `SetPrivacyModeUseCase`). On-device (a paired staging account, [[test-account-credentials]], since Couple is involved): tap the eye on Recurring → rule amounts mask, and it sits right of the calendar toggle; tap it on Manage → Net assets masks *and* Categories/Budgets amounts mask on the other two tabs without a second tap; tap it on Couple → Spending *and* Debts both mask from one control; confirm the tab row reads **Spending | Debts** and the Couple first-visit tour's copy matches the new label; then confirm the flag is genuinely global — mask on Manage, navigate to Records/Analysis, amounts are already hidden there too, and Settings → Finance shows the switch already on.
- **Build outcome:** built to the plan above, plus one mid-build addition and two bugs found + fixed on-device.
  - **Mid-build addition (Alvin, during the build):** Analysis' header also reordered — the "Net assets" figure (previously rightmost, after the bell) moved to the **left** of the bell, with the eye taking the new rightmost slot. This needed a new `leadingActions` slot on `PlayfulScreenTitle` (rendered before the bell, alongside the existing trailing `actions` slot) — a generalization that also unblocks [Item 17](#item-17--records-header-cleanup-drop-the--overflow-reorder-to-filter--bell--eye)'s planned filter-before-bell reorder, so that item no longer needs to add the slot itself. Analysis' own `togglePrivacyMode`/`privacyModeEnabled` plumbing (ViewModel + UiState) was deleted the same way as the four VMs above.
  - **Bug found (on-device, first pass):** the fully-paired branch of `CoupleScreen.kt`'s `PlayfulScreenTitle` (the one actually reached by every paired user, covering both Spending and Debts) was missing `actions = { PrivacyEyeAction() }` — only the unpaired branch got it. Paired users — the entire audience of this screen — had no eye control at all. One-line fix; re-verified clean.
  - **Scope gap found (on-device, first pass):** Budgets' own `MonthStepper` row carried a second, separate eye button pre-dating this slice, not mentioned in the plan above (only Accounts' Net-assets card eye was known). Left in place it would have meant two working eyes on the Manage screen. Removed it (+ its now-dead `BudgetsViewModel.togglePrivacyMode`/`BudgetsUiState.privacyModeEnabled`), leaving the Manage header eye as Budgets' only control, same as Accounts/Categories.
  - **On-device verified (dispatched, two passes):** first pass covered Recurring/Manage/Couple/Debts/Analysis/global-flag/tour-copy and found the two issues above; second pass re-verified both fixes in isolation. No bugs remaining; no crashes/ANRs either pass.

## Item 18 — Justify the module tab rows (equal-width chips, edge to edge)

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-28. **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — a one-modifier change repeated three times, no grill needed. **No schema/Room change.** Independent of [Item 16](#item-16--privacy-eye-becomes-a-standard-top-bar-action-recurring-manage-couple--combined-tab-renamed-spending)/[Item 17](#item-17--records-header-cleanup-drop-the--overflow-reorder-to-filter--bell--eye), but it edits `CoupleScreen.kt` and `ManageScreen.kt` which Item 16 also touches — **build after Item 16** to avoid two slices fighting over the same files.
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-28):** the three module tab rows — Couple (Spending · Debts), Analysis (Donut · Flow · Calendar), Manage (Accounts · Categories · Budgets) — should be **"justified"**, i.e. fill the row's full width instead of packing left and leaving dead space on the right.
- **Confirmed reading (asked before booking, 2026-07-28):** "justified" = **equal-width chips**, each `Modifier.weight(1f)`, together spanning the row and flush at both edges — the standard segmented-control look. **Not** `Arrangement.SpaceBetween` (chips keep their natural width, gaps stretch): that was shown and rejected, mainly because Couple has only **two** chips where the others have three, so stretching the gap would leave a large hole in the middle of that row. Equal-width was also chosen over an inconsistent "3-chip rows only" variant — **all three rows justify, Couple included**, so tab rows look the same in every module.
- **Change:** all three rows are the identical construction today — a `fillMaxWidth` `Row` with `horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)` holding text-hugging `PlayfulChip`s. Pass `modifier = Modifier.weight(1f)` to each chip at [ManageScreen.kt:109](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/manage/presentation/ManageScreen.kt#L109), [AnalysisScreen.kt:260](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisScreen.kt#L260), and [CoupleScreen.kt:126](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/couple/presentation/CoupleScreen.kt#L126). The 8dp spacing, the 22dp row padding, and [PlayfulChip](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/ui/PlayfulChip.kt)'s own shape/animation/44dp-min-height recipe all stay as-is — `PlayfulChip` already takes a `modifier` param and centers its content, so no change to the component itself.
  - **Scope is exactly these three rows.** `PlayfulChip` has ~10 other call sites — the Analysis **range** selector ([AnalysisScreen.kt:352](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/analysis/presentation/AnalysisScreen.kt#L352)), `TransactionFilterSheet`, Savings/Categories/Accounts/Budgets/PartnerDebt filter rows, `CoachMark`'s buttons, `AppearanceScreen` — **none of which are module tab rows, and none of which change.** Filter chips are a variable-length set that should hug their text; justifying them would be wrong.
  - **Risk to check at build time, not skip:** with fixed 1/3 widths, the longest label in each row ("Categories", "Calendar") has the least slack, and `PlayfulChip`'s `Text` sets **no `maxLines`/`overflow`** — so on a narrow screen or at a large system font scale it can wrap to two lines and jog the row's height. If that happens, add `maxLines = 1` (+ `TextOverflow.Ellipsis`, or drop the chip's 14dp horizontal padding when weighted) rather than shortening any label.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` green. **No tier-1 tests** (pure layout modifier, no domain/data logic). On-device: all three rows sit flush to both margins with equal-width chips; the selected-chip accent fill, the corner-radius morph on select, and the swipe-to-change-page ↔ tab-tap sync all still work in each module; the Analysis **range** row directly above the tabs is visibly *unchanged* (still hugging) — that contrast is the check that the scope was right; check a **small phone at the largest font scale** for label wrapping per the risk above; and confirm the Couple row's two half-width chips don't read as oversized once seen on a real device (Alvin's call — if they do, that's a follow-up tweak, not a re-litigation of the layout).

## Item 19 — Make Records' "Coming up" card collapsible

- **Status:** PLANNED — booked 2026-07-28. **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — a local UI-state + persisted-preference change following an existing in-repo precedent; no grill needed. **No schema/Room/Supabase change (Room stays v31).**
- **Request (Alvin, 2026-07-28):** the "Coming up" recurring preview on Records should be **collapsible/expandable**. Reasoning given: a user with many recurring rules gets a block of forecast rows eating the top of the Records screen before they reach their actual ledger.
- **Sanity check on the premise (worth stating, doesn't change the ask):** the card is already capped — [ComingUpViewModel](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/ComingUpViewModel.kt) takes a 14-day window and `PREVIEW_LIMIT = 5` rows, so "too many recurring" tops out at 5 rows, not an unbounded list. But 5 rows + a header is still a real chunk of a phone's first screen, and it stacks **below** the "To confirm" card ([TransactionsScreen.kt:242-252](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/TransactionsScreen.kt#L242-L252)) — so on a busy week the ledger genuinely starts below the fold. The ask stands; it just isn't unbounded, which means **collapse, not pagination or a smaller cap**, is the right fix.
- **Change:**
  - Add a collapsed/expanded state to [ComingUpCard](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/components/ComingUpCard.kt). **Collapsed ≠ hidden:** keep the header row visible with the item count and a chevron (e.g. "Coming up · 5" + ⌄), so the card stays discoverable and re-expandable. Only the occurrence rows collapse. Animate with the same reduced-motion respect the rest of the Playful Pop components use (`LocalReducedMotion`).
  - **Persist the choice** rather than using bare `remember`/`rememberSaveable` — a user who collapses it wants it to stay collapsed next launch, not re-expand on every cold start. Follow the existing local-UI-preference precedent: a DataStore-backed flag alongside [OnboardingRepository](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/onboarding/domain/repository/OnboardingRepository.kt)'s `observePairingCardDismissed`/`observeWidgetNudgeLastShownAt` (same shape: `observeComingUpCollapsed(): Flow<Boolean>` + `setComingUpCollapsed(Boolean)`), surfaced through `ComingUpUiState`. **Default = expanded** (today's behavior) — an opt-out, not an opt-in.
  - **Locked/teaser path unchanged:** when `RECURRING_FORECAST` is enforced without access the card is already a one-line count-only upsell teaser ([ComingUpCard.kt:60-66](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/components/ComingUpCard.kt#L60-L66)) — there is nothing to collapse, so the teaser keeps rendering as-is and ignores the flag. The empty-window early-return (`if (state.items.isEmpty()) return`) also stays: an empty card must self-hide entirely, not become a collapsed header for nothing.
  - **Explicitly out of scope:** the **"To confirm"** card ([PendingConfirmationsCard](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/recurring/presentation/components/PendingConfirmationsCard.kt)) directly above it. It has the same footprint problem, but it is **actionable** (rules waiting on the user) where "Coming up" is purely informational — letting a user permanently collapse pending confirmations means they silently stop confirming. Not folded in; raise it separately if Alvin wants it.
  - **Generalize only if a second caller appears:** build the collapse inside `ComingUpCard` first. If "To confirm" or another card later wants the same behavior, *then* lift the header+chevron into a reusable `core/ui` collapsible-card wrapper — don't build the abstraction for one caller.
- **Verify:** `assembleStagingDebug` + `testStagingDebugUnitTest` green. **Tier-1 tests: not required** for the Composable itself, but if the collapsed flag lands on `OnboardingRepository`/its impl, extend the existing repository test alongside it (data-layer logic, per the testing policy). On-device: collapse the card → rows disappear, header + count remain, the ledger moves up; **kill and relaunch the app** → still collapsed (this is the check that distinguishes a real fix from `rememberSaveable`); expand → rows return; navigate Records → another tab → back and confirm the state holds; confirm an **empty** upcoming window still hides the card completely rather than showing a collapsed shell; and confirm "To confirm" above it is untouched.
